bFGF improved the viability and survival of skin and soft tissues after irradiation.
the local injection of bFGF improved the survival of skin and soft tissues after irradiation.
bFGF improved the tissue viability and maintained the tissue survival after immediate irradiation.

the use of bFGF for the treatment of radiation damage to the tissue.
the use of bFGF as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of radiation‐exposed skin and soft tissue in the early phase.
the use of bFGF as a therapeutic agent for skin and soft tissue damage after irradiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bFGF can be a promising candidate for the prevention of skin and soft‐tissue radiation damage and for tissue preservation.
the bFGF‐mediated tissue‐preservation method is useful for the treatment of radiation‐exposed skin and soft tissue.
the local administration of bFGF is a safe and feasible method to enhance the viability of skin and soft tissues after irradiation, and that it is a promising approach for clinical use in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bFGF has the ability to improve and maintain the viability of skin and soft tissues in the early stages of radiation‐exposed tissues.
the bFGF is a potent growth factor for radiation exposure and that the expander with bFGF is useful for the treatment of radiation‐exposed skin and soft tissue in a clinical setting.

the local application of bFGF to tissue exposed to radiation may be a useful treatment option for tissue preservation and wound healing.
the use of basic fibroblasts growth factor (b‐FGF) in combination with tissue expansion can help to preserve the tissue and improve the clinical course of radiation‐damaged tissue.
